title: How to Choose the Right AI Model

scenes.text: There are hundreds of AI models out there. Big, small, open, closed, cheap, expensive. [1] How do you pick the right one for your project? [2] Today, a simple checklist that puts together everything we've learned.

Start with the task. [1] What exactly must it do? Chat, write code, read images, or classify tickets? [2] How good must it be? A typo in a fun caption is fine, but not in a medical summary. [3] And what are the limits, like budget, speed, and privacy?

[1] Now, match the needs. [2] Need top reasoning? A large frontier model. [3] Huge volume of simple jobs? A small, cheap model. [4] Private data? An open model on your own servers. [5] Photos or voice? A multimodal model. [6] Long documents? A big context window.

Then test like a pro. [1] Shortlist two or three models. [2] Build a small test set, of 30 to 50 real examples. [3] Run all models on the same set. [4] Compare quality, cost, and speed. [5] Pick the cheapest one that clears your quality bar.

Remember, it's always a trade-off, a triangle of quality, cost, and speed. [1] Push for top quality, and cost goes up. [2] Push for speed and low cost, and quality may drop. [3] The balance point depends on your task.

data.heading: The trade-off triangle
settings: Small model: good enough for sorting tickets
Mid model: solid summaries at a fair price
Frontier model: best, but pricier and slower

scenes.text: Here's a common myth. [1] People think they should always use the newest, biggest model. [2] Often, a smaller or older model does the job just as well, for a fraction of the price. And you can mix models, for different steps.

data.myth: Always use the newest, biggest model.
data.fact: A smaller or older model often does the job just as well, for a fraction of the price.

scenes.text: Here's a real example. A customer support app might use three models. [1] A small model sorts incoming tickets. [2] A mid model drafts the replies, using RAG. [3] And a top model handles only the tricky cases.
Quick quiz! After testing, which model should you usually pick? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] The cheapest one that meets your quality bar!
